items.description: Painting the disturbed wall area and closing the wall opening
items.rationale: Repair of the affected wall area after leak is covered under 7.1.5 and 7.1.7; only the disturbed area is indemnified, not the whole room. Reference Case 36 (cleaning/repainting affected area) suggests similar work is indemnified.
One travel/call-out charge per contractor per invoice is indemnified (7.1.7(f)). Reference Case 27 and 36 show typical rates.
Consumable installation material used in the repair is covered (7.1.7(c)). Reference Case 32 and 34 show similar items indemnified.
Replacement pipe for the affected section is covered as part of the repair (7.1.7(c)), but only for the damaged length. 1 m is plausible for a wall section.
Replacement of insulation removed to access/repair the pipe is covered (7.1.7(c)). Reference Case 32 supports this.
Labour for pipe repair is covered (7.1.7(g)). Reference Case 32 and 34 show similar rates.
Flat-rate deployment of measuring equipment for leak detection or moisture measurement is covered once per drying/repair operation (7.1.7(e)). Reference Case 36 and 32.
Labour for leak detection, opening wall, repair, and closing up is covered (7.1.7(g)). Reference Case 27 and 36 show similar work and rates.
Only the first travel/call-out charge per contractor per invoice is indemnified (7.1.7(f)); second charge is excluded.
Drying necessary before repair is covered (7.1.7(b)). Reference Case 36 and 27 show similar charges indemnified.
Reusable contractor tools are excluded (7.1.8(b)), but minor consumable blades may be allowed if used up in the repair. Reference Case 32 and 34 suggest low indemnity.
Gunmetal fittings (e.g., connectors) used in the pipe repair are covered as consumable installation material (7.1.7(c)). Reference Case 32 and 34.
If both lengths were needed for the repair of the affected section, both are covered (7.1.7(c)). If only one was needed, the second is not. Assume both were required for a typical wall run.
Replacement insulation for the repaired pipe is covered (7.1.7(c)). Reference Case 32.

If this is a duplicate of line 8, only the first is indemnified (7.1.8(c)). If it is for a separate, necessary part of the repair (e.g., second visit), it may be covered. Reference Case 27 and 36: assume both visits were needed.
